original_question: Let n >= 3, and let Omega and Omega' be bounded open subsets of R^n. Consider the class of Sobolev maps f in W^{1,p}(Omega, Omega') that arise as weak W^{1,p} limits of diffeomorphisms fk from Omega onto Omega'. Consider also the class of Sobolev maps f in W^{1,p}(Omega, Omega') that arise as strong W^{1,p} limits of diffeomorphisms fk from Omega onto Omega'. Are these two classes equal?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open problem 8: "Weak and strong closure of diffeomorphisms for n>2." ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core target very well: it is about higher dimensions (your n>=3 matches the paper's n>2), bounded open sets Omega and Omega' in R^n, Sobolev W^{1,p} convergence, diffeomorphisms Omega -> Omega', and whether weak and strong limit classes coincide. That is exactly the diffeomorphism closure question isolated in Section 3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))
missing_details: The paper phrases this as an equality of the sequential weak and strong W^{1,p}-closures of the class of diffeomorphisms, so the ambient closure formulation should be stated explicitly rather than only describing two informal classes of limit maps. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))

The exponent p should be explicitly quantified in the stand-alone question; the paper discusses the problem in the general W^{1,p} setting inherited from the introduction, not with p left implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))

To stay closest to the paper, the limit should be viewed as lying in the ambient Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Omega;R^n); the official formulation is about closures of the source class of diffeomorphisms, not about a pre-imposed codomain-restricted space W^{1,p}(Omega,Omega'). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))

It should be identified as the diffeomorphism version only, namely Open problem 8, and not merged with the parallel homeomorphism problem in Open problem 7. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))

The paper uses the higher-dimensional condition n>2 and places it against the known planar equality result discussed immediately before Open problems 7 and 8. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))
refined_question: Let n>2, let 1 <= p < infinity, and let Omega, Omega' be bounded open subsets of R^n. If D(Omega,Omega') denotes the class of diffeomorphisms f: Omega -> Omega', is the sequential weak W^{1,p}(Omega;R^n)-closure of D(Omega,Omega') equal to its strong W^{1,p}(Omega;R^n)-closure?
justification: Section 3 first introduces the weak-limit/strong-limit closure viewpoint for homeomorphisms and diffeomorphisms between bounded open sets, recalls that in the planar case these classes coincide, and then separates the higher-dimensional question into Open problem 7 for homeomorphisms and Open problem 8 for diffeomorphisms. Since your draft is specifically about diffeomorphisms, Open problem 8 is the nearest official formulation. I sharpened the wording by using the closure language actually suggested by Section 3, quantifying p, and removing the extra codomain restriction on the limit map. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01336v1))
